turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training observations with the highest measured yield strengths (all well below the 1051 MPa target) are isolated in composition–process space. Consequently a nearest-neighbour (or locally interpolating) regressor assigns a candidate the strength of its closest training neighbour; the five pool recipes that lie nearest those high-strength neighbours therefore receive the highest predicted values and are the closest to 1051 MPa.

- c079 is an extremely close match to the 908 MPa quench-and-temper AM point (identical heat-treatment/route, Co/V/Cu/aging nearly identical).  
- c017 and c094 sit next to the 864 MPa quench-and-temper wrought point (same categorical settings, only modest offsets in Cr/Ni/Mo).  
- c008 and c033 sit next to the 738 MPa quench-and-temper cast point (again identical categoricals and only small numeric offsets).

No other pool member is comparably close to any training example whose measured strength exceeds ~720 MPa, so the ranking by predicted proximity to 1051 MPa is unambiguous.

Final: c079, c017, c094, c008, c033
